newsitem.title: UK: Britain's Lloyd Webber to sell wine collection.
newsitem.headline: Britain's Lloyd Webber to sell wine collection.

text.p: British composer Andrew Lloyd Webber will sell his wine collection of 18,000 bottles at auction in May and it is expected to fetch more than two million pounds ($3.3 million), auctioneers Sotheby's said on Wednesday.
The London sale of what Sotheby's claim is "undoubtedly the greatest single wine collection ever to appear at auction" will take place on May 21.

"In terms of quality, choice and quantity it represents the wine lover's dream cellar," Sotheby's said in a statement. "Virtually every bottle falls into the category of the world's most desirable wine."

Lloyd Webber, 48, is selling his cellar because his enthusiasm for wine has "somewhat overwhelmed" him, Sotheby's said. "He realises he has collected enough wine for at least five lifetimes," it said.
His cellar is essentially French and the sale will include large quantities of the coveted 1982 Bordeaux vintages.
Among the jewels of the collection are 12 magnums of Petrus 1947, 10 bottles of Lafite 1945 and four cases of 1947 Latour a Pomerol.

"If Bacchus had a cellar, this would be it," said Sothebys. Lloyd Webber is among Britain's richest people having earned a fortune from writing and producing hit musicals such as Jesus Christ Superstar, Evita and Phantom of the Opera. ($1=.6120 Pound)
